examples.title: In a Button
examples.code:
<Buttons>
  <Button color="primary" aria-keyshortcuts="Control+S">
    Save
    <Kbd.Group ml="2">
      <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>
      <Kbd>S</Kbd>
    </Kbd.Group>
  </Button>
  <Button aria-keyshortcuts="Escape">
    Cancel
    <Kbd ml="2">Esc</Kbd>
  </Button>
</Buttons>

examples.title: Mac and Windows
Compound (dot-notation) usage
examples.code:
<Paragraph>
  Press{' '}
  <Kbd.Group>
    <Kbd label="Command">⌘</Kbd>
    <Kbd>Shift</Kbd>
    <Kbd>P</Kbd>
  </Kbd.Group>{' '}
  on a Mac, then{' '}
  <Kbd.Group separator="then">
    <Kbd>G</Kbd>
    <Kbd>I</Kbd>
  </Kbd.Group>
  .
</Paragraph>

accessibility:
- **Markup:** a key is a `<kbd>`, and a combination is an outer `<kbd>` around one `<kbd>` per key,
  the form the [HTML standard](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-kbd-element)
  gives for keys pressed together. Neither adds a role or any `aria-*`, and neither takes focus.
- **What a screen reader hears:** nothing marks a `<kbd>` as a key, so a screen reader reads the
  text inside it like the rest of the sentence. The separator is text with a space either side,
  so `Ctrl`, `Shift` and `P` read as "Ctrl plus Shift plus P" and never run together into one word.
- **Symbols:** a glyph like ⌘, ⌥, ⇧, ⌃ or ⏎ needs a `label`. It goes in visually hidden text,
  with the glyph hidden from assistive tech. Copying the key copies the label along with the glyph.
- **Never `aria-label` on a key:** ARIA in HTML prohibits naming a `<kbd>`, so nothing obliges a
  screen reader to read one. That's why `label` renders text instead.
- **The shortcut lives on the control:** put
  [`aria-keyshortcuts`](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#aria-keyshortcuts) on the button or
  link the shortcut triggers, in UI Events key names: `Control+Shift+P`, with `Meta` for ⌘ and
  `Alt` for Option. `Kbd` is only the hint people see.
- **Contrast:** the key's text is the color of the text around it and its fill is faint, so the
  text keeps the contrast its paragraph, button or tooltip already has.
- **Forced colors:** the key is drawn with a border, not a shadow, so it still looks like a key in
  Windows high contrast mode.
- **Selectable:** the text can be selected and copied, so people can copy a shortcut out of a help
  page.
summary: The `Kbd` component renders a `<kbd>` drawn as a keycap, for a key the reader presses. It only shows the key: it doesn't listen for it. The key takes its colors from the text it sits in, and its size in `em`, so it fits a paragraph, a title or a filled button as it is, and `textSize` sizes it outright. For a combination or a sequence, put the keys in a `Kbd.Group`. What tells assistive tech a control has a shortcut is `aria-keyshortcuts` on that control, with `Kbd` as the hint people see next to it.

props.name: children
props.description: The key as it's printed on the keyboard: a word (`Ctrl`, `Esc`), a letter, or a symbol (`⌘`).

props.name: label
props.description: What a screen reader says in place of a symbol, in your app's language: `label="Command"` on `⌘`. The symbol is hidden from assistive tech with `aria-hidden`, and the label is read in its place, from text that's visually hidden. Use it for a glyph that isn't a word, such as `⌘`, `⌥`, `⇧`, `⌃` or `⏎`, and leave it off a key written as a word. Copying the key copies the label along with the glyph. Don't reach for `aria-label` instead: ARIA in HTML prohibits naming a `<kbd>`, so nothing obliges a screen reader to read it.

props.name: textColor
props.description: Text color helper. The key's edge and fill are mixed from its text color, so they follow it.

props.name: bgColor
props.description: Background color helper. It replaces the key's faint fill.

parts.catchAll: All standard HTML attributes and Bulma helper props

parts.summary: Keys pressed together or one after another, in the outer `<kbd>` HTML gives a combination, with the separator between each pair as text. It doesn't wrap in the middle and isn't drawn as a key itself. It sets no font size, so the keys in it are the size of a key on its own.

props.name: children
props.description: The keys, a `Kbd` each, in the order they're pressed. The group renders the outer `<kbd>` around them, so it doesn't go inside a `Kbd` of its own, and it puts the separator between them, so don't type one: a `+` of your own doubles up. A child that renders nothing (`null`, `false`) gets no separator.

props.name: separator
props.description: What goes between the keys, shown and read aloud, with a space either side. Use `'then'` for a sequence pressed one key after another. It's a string because a screen reader has to read it.

props.name: textColor
props.description: Text color helper. The keys and separators inside follow it.

parts.catchAll: All standard HTML attributes and Bulma helper props
